response.reason: NL1 is descriptive scope-setting with no independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes a continuous task obligation (state_action) and a cardinality obligation over three state areas (region/domain ambiguous, kept unresolved with alternative reading), plus containment of the swarm operating within those areas. NL3 establishes an interception-triggered transition endpoint into a formation-adjustment state, with event 'intercepted'. NL4 establishes two chained obligations: (a) a task-assignment-triggered transition into attack state, with event/guard split for 'task assignment information is received', and (b) a variable-delta effect on UAV count decreasing after completing the attack, tied to a completion/termination-like phrase but not explicit termination of the whole mission, so kept as effect on variable count rather than manufacturing a termination contract, since NL2 already reserves 'mission completed' as the actual termination boundary condition governing the continuous NL2 activity.

result.reason: The closed FCSTM shows a root machine whose only outgoing initial edge targets a plain leaf state InitialState (line 20), which has zero outgoing transitions. Region1 and Region2 -- the two composites that own all authored operating behavior (TargetSearch/FormationAdjustment and AttackReady/Attack) -- have no incoming edge from the root and are entirely unreachable from the top-level initial entry, per inspection_equivalent_facts.reachability, verify_facts non_proved reachability rows, and reference_inspection_facts diagnostics (W_UNREACHABLE_STATE x4, W_DEADLOCK_LEAF x1). All four declared events have consumers only inside these unreachable regions, so none of the four event-consumer contracts (search interception, formation-adjusted return, task-assignment, attack-complete) can ever fire from the closed model's reachable state set. semantic_adjudication.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.reachability (TargetSearch reachable_from_initial=false); reference_inspection_facts W_DEADLOCK_LEAF at InitialState; verify_facts deadlock check for InitialState status=refuted, outgoing_count=0
semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL2 contract requires the swarm to continuously perform target-search activity. The exact closed model shows the root machine's only reachable state is InitialState with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING at line 20), while TargetSearch and its entire owning Region1/Region2 structure are unreachable from root, so continuous target-search activity can never be entered. The candidate's own strongest_rebuttal notes TargetSearch has its own outgoing transition and is not itself a local dead end, but this addresses only TargetSearch's local well-formedness, a different property than whether the root ever retains/enters this activity; per the property-preserving protocol a locally well-formed state does not rebut the exact obligation that the activity be retained from root. The rebuttal is therefore defeated, though the sibling reachability/deadlock candidates capture the related but distinct defects.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: TargetSearch itself has an outgoing transition (tr_0003/transition:line:10) and is not a local dead end, so its own state-action content could be argued to be intact.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The UAV swarm must continuously perform target-search tasks as an ongoing operating activity prior to mission completion.

This produces independent behavioral-consequence issues: (1) the UAV swarm's overall operating scope (root) never reaches the target-search sub-structure, violating the derived initial_entry/root-reachability obligation; (2) the InitialState leaf is a deterministic deadlock frontier (V1) that blocks progress, undermining the continuous state_action obligation for target search; (3) the NL3 interception->formation-adjustment endpoint's source state is unreachable, so the required transition can never be exercised even though the edge itself exists in Region1; (4) the NL4 flight->attack endpoint is likewise never reachable; (5) event-consumer coverage fails for all four events since declared consumers have zero reachable_consumer_transition_refs. I preserve the exact endpoint/action/effect contracts themselves as satisfied at the local edge level (edges tr_0003/TargetSearch->FormationAdjustment and tr_0006/AttackReady->Attack exist with correct triggers) and instead attach the reachability defect to its own derived contract per the frontier discipline, plus one V1 deadlock candidate and one event-consumer-coverage candidate to avoid conflating distinct properties.
